segments.text: Introduced by Christian Heinrich von Nagel in eighteen thirty-six, X nine is the Mittenpunkt— literally the middle point: the concurrence of the three lines joining the excenters J sub a, J sub b, and J sub c to the corresponding side midpoints M sub a, M sub b, and M sub c.

segments.text: Geometrically, X nine is the symmedian point of the excentral triangle. Its trilinear distances are proportional to the semiperimeter excesses, s minus a, to s minus b, to s minus c, and its barycentric areas are a times s minus a, to b times s minus b, to c times s minus c. On the central lines layer, X nine lies at the intersection of line X one X six, line X two X seven, and the Orthocenter–Spieker line X four X ten.
